chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Maruf ibn Kharbouz, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) led the people in the morning prayer in Iraq. When he finished, he preached to them, wept, and made them weep from the fear of Allah.

Then he said: 'By Allah, I lived with a group of people in the era of my friend, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Indeed, they would become shaggy, dusty, and slim-bellied by morning and evening. Between their eyes was like the hoof of a goat [from prostration]. They would spend the night for their Lord prostrating and standing, rotating between their feet and their foreheads, whispering to their Lord, and asking Him to free their necks from the Fire. By Allah, I saw them with all this, and they were fearful and anxious.'

key_terms.خَائِفُونَ مُشْفِقُونَ: Fearful and anxious (in awe of Allah)
key_terms.كَرُكَبِ الْمِعْزَى: Like the hoof of a goat (referring to the mark of prostration)

ai.seo_question: What were the physical and spiritual signs of the companions of the Prophet according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the profound spiritual intensity of the early companions, using vivid physical descriptions like 'shaggy hair' and 'calloused foreheads' to signify their deep immersion in night prayers (*Qiyam*). It underscores the Shia emphasis on *Khushu'* (humility and focus) and the balance between outward asceticism and inner fear of Allah, a trait exemplified by Imam Ali’s own emotional leadership during his sermons in Iraq.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Marouf Bin Kharbouz, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws prayed Salāt with the people (leading them), in Al-Iraq. So when heasws finished, heasws preached to them, and heasws wept and made them weep from fear of Allahazwj.

Then heasws said: ‘But, by Allahazwj! Iasws lived with a group of people in the era of myasws friend Rasool-Allahsaww, and they, in the morning and evening, becoming shaggy, dusty, slim-bellied, between their eyes was like the hoof of a goat due to their prostrations to their Lordazwj. They were staying awake at nights for their Lordazwj, prostrating and standing (for Salāt), rotating between their feet and their foreheads, whispering to their Lordazwj, and asking Himazwj to Free their necks from the Fire. By Allahazwj! Iasws had seen them being with this, and they were fearful, anxious’.
en.sarwar: 21. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Ma’ruf ibn Kharrabuz from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Once Amir al-Mu’minin (Ali ibn abu Talib) (a.s.) prayed the morning prayer with people in Iraq. After prayer he gave a speech on having fear of Allah. He wept and made people weep.

He then said, ‘By Allah, I lived with a people, in the times of my beloved one, the Messenger of Allah, who were ragged, dusty and slim-bellied. Between their eyes it looked like the hooves of a goat. They spent the night in prostration and in standing position before their Lord, only resting on their feet or forehead. They whispered to their Lord to set their necks free from the fire and, by Allah, I saw them in such condition and they still were afraid and anxious (because of the next life).”’
